text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- Swiss Minister Flavio Cotti said that U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato is not interested in the facts or fair discussions regarding Switzerland's role in World War Two. He added that no tax money will flow into the special funds established in Switzerland for Holocaust victims.

- Swiss Ambassador Thomas Borer said in a speech in a New York synagogue at the weekend that the majority of Swiss people were courageous, believed in democratic values, and were against the terror of the Nazi regime in World War Two.
- U.S. group Burston Marsteller will take acquire a majority stake in PR and advertising agency Jaeggi Communications. Jaeggi is headquartered in Berne and Zurich and employs 35 people.
- Unigestion Holding boosted consolidated net profit to 41.7 million Swiss francs in 1996 compared to 11.1 million francs in 1995.
- The Swiss People's Party gained 11 more seats at the weekend's elections in Canton Aargau.
- The majority of voters in Zurich voted against a people's initiative calling for a car-free inner city last weekend.
- Citizens in Canton Grisons voted in favour of obligatory Italian lessons for three years for primary school children starting from the fourth grade.
- Jet Aviation is taking over ground service for United Airlines at the Zurich airport starting May 1.
- Over 1,000 people gathered in Zurich to listen to Christoph Blocher, a Zurich politician and president of the Swiss People's Party, defend Switzerland's actions in World War Two.
